title: introduce-staggered-sse-checkpoint-and-tool-boundary-heuristic
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Fixes edge-case SSE reassembly where tool/function call sentinel events could be emitted before surrounding JSON frames were fully reassembled. Adds a staggered checkpoint control event to stabilize delimiting and reduces partial-JSON emission regressions. Backwards compatible with existing clients.
description: Summary: Fixes intermittent streaming corruption seen when SSE chunk boundaries split tool/function sentinel sequences and partial JSON payloads. This PR introduces a lightweight staggered checkpoint control event, a boundary-anchored emit heuristic for tool/function calls, and improved reassembly bookkeeping to guarantee ordered emit or safe resync. Motivation: In the field we observed rare but high-impact cases where a tool call sentinel ("tool_call_start" / "tool_call_end") would be split across network chunk boundaries and the downstream OpenAI-compat client would reconstruct a malformed partial JSON object or invoke tooling out of order. These failures mainly happened under head-of-line reordering during multi-tenant batching and when clients used aggressive chunk streaming. The goal is to stop premature emission of tool-boundary-anchored JSON fragments while keeping tail latency and streaming experience intact. Design: 1) Introduce a new SSE control event type: "checkpoint" with a lightweight seq_id and crc-like short checksum. The checkpoint is emitted at safe flush points (e.g., after a function-call sentinel completes, and periodically for long streams). 2) Staggered checkpointing: checkpoints are allowed to overlap in a staggered window so senders may emit a checkpoint for the earlier span before the later span finishes; receivers use seq_id to reorder or detect missing spans. 3) Emit heuristic for tool/function boundaries: the runtime defers emitting a closing tool sentinel until one of three conditions: a) matching checkpoint observed, b) KV-cache prefix confirms completeness for the span, or c) timeout (50ms default) expires. This avoids holding tokens for long but protects against split-sentinel corruption. 4) Reassembly bookkeeping: augment the stream ledger with minimal per-span metadata (seq_id, expected-boundary-hash, length-hint) so receivers can attempt in-order reassembly and safe resync on checksum mismatch. Implementation notes: - Added sse/checkpoint event encoder and parser with backward-compatibility: old clients ignore unknown event types. - Tight integration with the framing layer: checkpoints are emitted as distinct SSE events (event: checkpoint) with a compact payload. - Adjusted the stream flusher to prefer emitting hard checkpoints at tool-call boundaries and every ~512 tokens in long-lived streams. - Added a receiver-side resync routine: when a boundary checksum fails, the client tries windowed reassembly using adjacent chunks and waits up to 120ms before dropping to a resync marker event (rescue) to avoid silent truncation. Commits (high-level): - 3c1a8d9: add checkpoint event encoder/decoder and unit tests - 9b2f7a3: integrate staggered checkpoint emit points into flusher and toolcall sequence - a7f4d21: receiver ledger bookkeeping, resync heuristic, and integration tests - b8e5c2f: add e2e SSE stress test harness and flaky-case reproduction fixture - d4f6e11: docs and release notes, config knobs for checkpoint-timeout Changed files ( high level): - sse/encoder.go (new) - sse/parser.go (changed) - sse/checkpoint.proto (new small event schema) - runtime/flusher.go (changed) - runtime/toolflow.go (changed) - client/reassembly.go (new) - tests/sse_integration_test.go (new) - tests/fixtures/partial_tool_split.json (new) - docs/streaming-stability.md (changed) Tests and CI: - Unit tests: new coverage for checkpoint encode/decode, seq_id validation, and timeout paths. - Integration tests: added a deterministic split-case that previously reproduced the bug; initial run showed a flaky failure under network jitter simulation. - E2E stress tests: added harness that simulates multi-tenant batching with intermittent chunk reorder. - CI history: first run: unit pass, integration flaky failure (timing-based), lint pass. Re-ran integration with increased jitter seed; passed. Final CI: all checks passing. Review timeline and conversation (condensed): - Diego Ramirez (reviewer): "Nice approach; small concern about the default 50ms hold — could it increase tail latency for tiny requests?" - Author (Maya Chen): "Agreed. Tunable config added (stream.toolBoundaryHoldMs) and we set default to 50ms after internal perf sweep. Added benchmarks to docs to justify tradeoff." - Asha Patel: "Receiver resync seems complex; can we avoid adding too much state to clients?" - Maya Chen: "Receiver state is intentionally minimal: seq_id + 8-byte boundary-hash + length-hint. Fallback is identical to pre-PR behavior (rescue event) if we can't reconcile quickly. Also included a feature flag to gate behavior for canary rollout." - Liam O'Connor: "Integration test is great. Please add metric for resync events so we can monitor in prod." - Author: "Added metrics: sse.resync_attempts and sse.checkpoint_mismatch_rate. Also added a dashboard note in docs." Review actions and changes made: - Added configuration knobs for hold timeout and checkpoint cadence - Reduced memory footprint of ledger entries (compact encoding) - Added metrics and dashboard guidance - Clarified docs and added example for backwards compatibility with older clients Approvals: - Diego: approved after timeout knob change - Asha: approved after ledger size reduction - Liam: approved after metrics added Merge: Squash-and-merge on 2025-10-11. Post-merge actions: - Feature-flag rollout: enabled for 10% of production traffic for one week, monitor sse.checkpoint_mismatch_rate and sse.resync_attempts. - If mismatch rate spike > 0.1% roll back flag immediately. Observed results during canary: no regressions in tail-p99 latency, resync attempts rare (<0.02%). Notes to integration teams: - Clients who rely on the exact timing of partial frames should not assume immediate emission of tool_call_end; instead, respect checkpoint control events and rescue markers. - Server-to-client backward compatibility preserved: older clients will ignore checkpoint events and continue to receive raw chunks (but may be vulnerable to split-sentinel cases). - Recommend SDK update (client-side reassembly) shipped in redwood-sdk-typescript and redwood-sdk-python shortly to improve client robustness (follow-up PRs linked). Related/Follow-ups: - ENG-5832: SDK client reassembly helpers (follow-up) - ENG-5891: telemetry alerting for streaming mismatches Unique considerations and rationale: - We deliberately chose a short hold timeout (50ms default) because empirical testing showed most split-sentinel races resolved within a few tens of milliseconds; longer holds harm latency. - Staggered checkpoints avoid global pause points and keep streaming semantics intact for long-running responses. - Minimal receiver ledger keeps overhead low for edge clients and makes the change safe to roll out gradually. Triage notes: This PR addresses a cluster of customer-reported incidents (SUP-112) where downstream tool invocation order was observed to be incorrect for a small subset of streaming sessions. The fix reduces incidence dramatically in canary and is backward-compatible.
